newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW drought declared area up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW drought declared area up sharply.

text.p: The area of drought in the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) had increased to 40 percent from 13 percent a month before, state Agriculture Minister Richard Amery said in a statement.
The major increase in the drought-declared area was causing grain producers to become concerned about winter crop production, he said.
The only substantial rain received over the month was on the north coast, he said. The major grain growing areas of NSW needed rain now to allow winter crop sowing to proceed, he said.
If rain fell in the next four to six weeks it was estimated that more than four million hectares would be sown, a similar area to last year, he said.
But the longer farmers had to wait to sow crops, the greater the likelihood of lower yields, he said.

The National Climate Centre had advised that the rainfall outlook for the medium-term was for below average rainfall in much of NSW, with the Southern Oscillation Index falling rapidly in recent weeks, he said.
